findings.summary: The Greek right-triangle explanation used awkward or incorrect side-ratio wording.
evidence: The previous paragraph described sine as αντίθετο έναντι της υποτείνουσας and used inconsistent side terminology.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the explanation with standard Greek terms for sine, cosine, tangent, opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse.

findings.summary: The sine formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression was sin(θ) = opposite / hypotenuse.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Greek side terminology.

findings.summary: The cosine formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression was cos(θ) = adjacent / hypotenuse.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Greek side terminology.

findings.summary: The tangent formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression was tan(θ) = opposite / adjacent.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Greek side terminology.

findings.summary: The worked sine example mistranslated sin as the Greek word for sin and used inconsistent side wording.
evidence: The previous expression contained αμαρτία(30°) instead of sin(30°).
findings.resolution: Restored the mathematical function notation and Greek side term.

findings.summary: The worked cosine example used an English function name and an inconsistent Greek side form.
evidence: The previous expression mixed γειτονικό with cos(30°) without consistent side terminology.
findings.resolution: Normalized the example to παρακείμενη and preserved cos(30°).

findings.summary: The inverse-sine formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression was θ = sin^-1(opposite / hypotenuse).
findings.resolution: Changed it to Greek side terminology.

findings.summary: The inverse-cosine formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression was θ = cos^-1(adjacent / hypotenuse).
findings.resolution: Changed it to Greek side terminology.

findings.summary: The inverse-tangent formula retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expression was θ = tan^-1(opposite / adjacent).
findings.resolution: Changed it to Greek side terminology.

findings.summary: The degrees-and-radians formula left the word radians in English.
evidence: The previous expression was 180° = π radians.

findings.summary: The heat-capacity conclusion incorrectly lowercased the first word after a sentence period.
evidence: The previous text contained kJ. μια πραγματική θερμάστρα.
findings.resolution: Capitalized Μια at the start of the second sentence.

findings.summary: The electrical-heating conclusion incorrectly lowercased the first word after a sentence period.
evidence: The previous text contained λεπτά. με απόδοση μεταφοράς.
findings.resolution: Capitalized Με at the start of the second sentence.

findings.summary: The length-conversion formulas left English unit names and decimal points in the Greek section.
evidence: The previous formulas used inch, foot, feet, and decimal points.
findings.resolution: Translated the unit names and normalized the decimal commas.
